data.name: ASSAULT GUNNERS HD EDITION
data.detailed_description:
ASSAULT GUNNERS HD EDITION põe-te ao comando da força de manutenção da paz DAT. Juntamente com três Battle Mechs aliados, tens de salvar os emigrantes da Terra e as colónias de Marte da ameaça da revolta ANTS. Quem ou o quê poderá estar por detrás desta ameaça contra Marte e a nova perfeita utopia para a Humanidade?

A versão independente de ASSAULT GUNNERS HD EDITION traz muitos conteúdos e oferece uma grande rejogabilidade com 35 missões completas com batalhas intensas, um modo de jogo com hordas conhecido como “Inferno Mode” que inclui 5 mapas e mais de 100 possibilidades de personalização de Mechs tanto para ti como para os teus aliados.

reviews.review:
This would be a mixed review if possible. While it is very short, generic and simple I did actually have fun playing it, however it's flaws mixed with its bugs drop this into a thumbs down. In short it really feels like an "Armored Core at home" but it does have neat things like group mechanics aswell as a meditative grindy gameplay loop.

First thing I noticed with the gameplay is that the control scheme is a little odd. I played using an Xbox remote, rather than mouse and keyboard, which is defaulted to being waaaaay faster. Anyways, you turn extremely slow by default. Slow enough that it does not feel very good. Also I thought that there wasn't a jump ability until maybe midway through my playthrough. Jump is actually very specifically standing still and double tapping to hold a shoulder button... it... it doesn't work most of the time, actually.

Mostly you'll be doing objective based missions if you aren't dead set on playing the endless survival mode. There's 20 missions for your first run of the story. After you complete this fully the first time you can unlock a further 15 side paths if you go back and replay missions for special objectives. I wish this all would of just been unlocked from the get-go and it was presented clearly what the exact unlock objective is. The text blurbs are rather vague about this. Also if you get the DLC the mission count gets brought up to 50.

Anyways, you do combat missions that come in a couple flavors. A lot of the time you just gotta defeat the enemies, but other times there will be a clear "go from point a to point b" type path. Other times it'll be a bit more open with your own choice of movement with a goal of capturing control nodes for one reason or another. Most of the time regardless of what's happening enemies will continue to spawn. Sometimes this leads into bosses which are mostly just a bigger more bullet spongy mechanical creature though late game ends up being GHOST in a mech similar to yours.

You'll get a choice of three weapons and a melee to blast through enemies with. When you blow them up they'll drop things for you like new weapons and parts to use in the hangar, health ups, or upgrade currencies. Before I mention the leveling up I'll go ahead and point out that the general cannon fodder enemies do come in a few varieties with tougher more armored HP clad variants. There's a few different walkers, some flyers, some bigger guys or smaller guys and even stationary artillery. Oh yeah, and most maps have some sort of crates you can blowup for drops, too.

Leveling up is done through the hangar. You can craft new parts or make the ones you have stronger before outfitting your team. DAT units themselves can be assembled by two parts, the body and the legs. After that you get options for main weapon, sub weapon, fist, and shoulder weapon. By far the largest section of customizability here is the additional parts which sadly have no visual difference, only stats. By endgame my mech could equip 15 different additional parts to really minmax specific stats out. Things like gravity wave barriers, muzzle brakes, blastproof coatings, boost cooling systems and so on. I will note that the DLC pack adds additional equipment though I'm unsure if their drops get included into the basegame content or only the DLC missions.

Additionally you can do all this for your entire team, four mechs in total. This is probably the greatest feature of this game that being your group of three additional teammates. As far as action oriented mech games go they seem to really like putting you in the solo position. You're the lone gunman on a mission with a mech - however here your meant to be part of a team and I gotta say I really enjoy the companionship even if I can't understand what they're saying. Even though the NPC pathing wasn't the greatest it was a great comfort to know that I had some friends to watch my back.

You can even set them up for different jobs within the group, like support or different attack types. There is a pretty decent weapon variety ingame. I tended to use the lock on shoulder mounted missiles or maybe the single shot laser the most. It seemed to shoot through multiple enemies at a time which was fun for me.

I've heard people talk about ASMR audio and how it creates a satisfying, calming, clicking in their brainstem and I think I get the same sorta feeling from the gameplay in this one. Despite being cheese-y, simple and rather generic it is still so satisfying to walk into a valley of 50 bots and slowly blast them away. I think a comparative feeling must be felt in those cleaning simulator games. Like lawnmowing sim or powerwasher sim. There is a mess to clean up and it feels good when the job is done but the mess here is a buncha angry robots and you clean them up with a machine gun.

Big issue right off the bat. I started experiencing significant slowdown when I'd launch a lotta missiles. At first I assumed this was a problem with the engine, being a handheld game port, and the smoke particle effect however I did fix the problem. It seems to be a trend that A LOT of specifically Japanese games give me where for some reason they default to booting up and using my INTERNAL GPU instead of the actual gaming graphics card. Easy enough fix for me since I've done it so many times at this point however this could be a huge and glaring problem for someone unaware.

I've talked about several issues this game has in their respective sections but I'll go ahead and recap incase you missed it. The story is pretty minimal and generic. It also lacks subtitles, which makes following the game difficult since the audio is only in Japanese. The gameplay controls are kinda wack, especially the jump. The enemy AI pretty much only vaguely walks toward you without skill or strategy. Your teammates AI is just as bad... The game seems to be created to replay a lot but lacks a substantial parts system or rewarding difficulty curve to really make you want to keep playing. Also its super short and the missions seem to re-use the same maps several times even though the whole game is less than 4 hours.

Honestly, its pretty okay for what it is. The shortcomings are pretty expected if you understand this is a game from overseas that was built for a handheld console 15 years ago. With that said even back then I'm sure it didn't hold up against its competitors in things like the Armored Core Portables and the most up to date HD port of this game significantly struggles to keep up with anything else that is on the current market. On the otherhand it's a pretty casual mech grinder experience that is fun if you just wanna chill and turn your brain off for a bit ripping through 'bots. At best its just okay which means the negatives stick out severely. Would it be recommendable as a PSVita game to play on the go? Sure. Is it recommendable as a PC game through Steam in 2026? Nope.
